## Owner input, 2026-09-10

**"ALL SYMBOLS count in Universal Symbology, which is the ultimate challenge."**

This is the falsification surface, and it is unusually strong for a system of
this kind: if every symbol must be derivable, then **any symbol the composition
rules cannot produce is a counterexample**. That makes the project refutable in
a way most symbolic systems are not, and it means coverage failures are findings
rather than gaps to paper over.

Recorded here because it should govern how discrepancies are treated: a case
that does not resolve is data, not an embarrassment.

**On triangle-vs-diamond (F12):** owner confirms the discrepancy is real and
unresolved, direction of resolution hinted as **(angle + line)**. Worth
re-examining Base 9 row 1 col 3 — read as a house/pentagon, but if the vertical
sides are an artefact of the closed-form rendering rather than part of the
construction, `^` + `_` is simply a triangle. **Re-check at higher resolution.**

findings.title: the cross-set: bar position on a stem encodes a 5-level scalar
findings.text:
`UniversalSymbology-CrossSet.png`. The crossbar's position along the stem gives
an ordered scale, and the same mechanism runs on both axes:

- vertical: Most High/Bright — High/Light — Center/Middle — Low/Dark — Most Low/Shadow
  (Ascend / Transcend / — / Descend / Subscend)
- horizontal: Leading/Far Left — Fore/Left — Center — Aft/Right — Trailing/Far Right
  (also Blue Team/Back … Red Team/Front, and elsewhere Blue Shift … Red Shift)

**Position along a line instantiating a total order** is precisely the Tier 1
example used in `docs/grounding/00-self-denotation.md` — written before reading
this sheet. The system already implements it. Independent arrival at the same
example is mild evidence the tier framing fits the material rather than being
imposed on it.

findings.title: Base 9 "Modals": closed shapes decompose into top/bottom halves
findings.text:
`UniversalSymbology-Base9_Modals.png`, a 3x3. Each cell shows a top half and a
bottom half, plus the closed shape they merge into. The three halves are the
three modalities from F4 — angular, curved, flat:

| top \ bottom | angular (v) | curved (u) | flat (|_|) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **angular** | diamond | pointed-top round-bottom | house/pentagon |
| **curved** | round-top pointed-bottom | circle | arch |
| **flat** | downward shield | flat-top U | square |

A generative rule for closed form: **shape = modality(top) x modality(bottom)**,
3 x 3 = 9. The pure diagonal gives diamond, circle, square.

**Possible inconsistency to resolve:** the AI primer's "Round / Sharp / Flat ->
Circle / Triangle / Square" trio does not sit cleanly on this basis — the pure
angular form here is a *diamond*, and no cell yields a plain triangle. Either
the two sheets work at different levels, or one supersedes the other. **Ask.**

findings.title: Base 16 "Redux" is a MORPHOLOGICAL PARADIGM, and this is the best evidence yet
findings.text:
`UniversalSymbology-Base16_Redux.png`, a 4x4 grid. Columns are base form;
rows are two binary geometric features — **closure** (open/closed) and **point**
(external / internal / absent):

| | Angle | Curve | Square | Point/Line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| open + external point | Act | Pass | Stat | Not (`!`) |
| closed + internal point | Actor | Passer | Stator | Note (`.`) |
| closed, no point | Action | Passion | Station | Notion (`x`) |
| open, no point | Active | Passive | Stative | Notive (`|`) |

**Two binary geometric features generate the four grammatical forms of a stem** —
bare verb, agent noun (-or), abstract noun (-ion), adjective (-ive) — and the
English morphology lines up across all four columns.

This is the strongest compositional evidence in the corpus so far, and it is
checkable by anyone who knows English morphology. It does not show the mapping is
*forced*; it shows it is *systematic*, which is a real and much more defensible
claim. **Candidate Tier 1** — the rule (closure x point -> grammatical category)
would have to be stated explicitly to qualify.

Consistent with F9: Notion = `x` (two angled lines), Notive = `|`, Note = `.`,
Not = `!` (line + point).

findings.title: the domain mappings are operational, not metaphysical
findings.text:
`UniversalSymbology-PointShapeLineWaveAngleCurve.png` maps each pair into
programming and physics vocabulary, not into semantic categories:

- Point&Shape → Init/Input (Instance), Cycle/Output (Object), Socket Input,
  Output Source
- Line&Wave → Value/Number (Constant), Range/String (Variable), Amperage DC,
  AC Voltage
- Angle&Curve → Run/Set (Act), Wait/Get (Pass), Flow/Pull, Life/Flux

`3CoreSymbolMergers` carries formula-shaped relations, one of which is simply
correct physics: **Power = Voltage × Amperage**. Also present:
System = Cycle/Period, Flux = Spark/Drain.

The MBTI axes appear too — Introversion/Extroversion on Point&Shape,
Judging/Perceiving on Line&Wave — with Intuition/Sensing/Thinking/Feeling on a
separate sheet. That is a borrowed taxonomy and should be checked for category
fit before being leaned on.

**Nothing is unread.** Every artifact in the corpus directory is named by at
least two findings. Re-derive by splitting this file on its `### F` headings and
searching each finding's text for the artifact's name; a count of 0 would mean
either an unread sheet or an alias this derivation does not know, and both are
worth chasing.

findings.title: composition produces recognisable glyphs (falsifiable)
findings.text:
`UniversalSymbology-SymbolFolds.png` gives three combination mechanics and their
outputs:

- **Reflection** (Patterns): two waves mirrored → **∞**; offset → **8**
- **Orientation** (Dimensions): two angled lines → **×**; two lines at right
  angles → **+**
- **Superposition**: line + point → **!**; line + circle → a cycle/intersect
  form, with distinct left and right variants (**chirality**)

This is a genuinely testable claim: the composition rules *predict existing
glyphs*. `!` really is a line above a point; `+` really is two crossed lines.
Whether the derivations are non-arbitrary across a larger set is checkable, and
would be evidence for the system in a way that assertion is not.

findings.title: full glyph names (six features, four labels each)
findings.text:
From the rotation table:

| feature | secondary | role | tertiary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Point | Vertex | [Core] | Dot / Period |
| Angle | Edge | [Alpha] | Intersect / Caret |
| Line | Link | [Order] | Segment / Dash |
| Wave | Path | [Chaos] | Pattern / Squiggle |
| Curve | Arc | [Omega] | Tangent / Breve |
| Shape | Contour | [Void] | Geometry / Circle |

Still no Existence/Relation/Quality/Process/Concept anywhere. F1 holds.

findings.title: CORRECTION to F2: it is not 4+2, or not only
findings.text:
F2 read the Mk3 grid as "4 base + 2 operators". The rotation table shows a
different split — the left margin divides the six 3+3:

- **Masculine / Action / Direction | Momentum** — Point, Angle, Line
- **Feminine / Passion / Spin | Spiral** — Wave, Curve, Shape

Both cuts exist and they are consistent rather than competing, because **each of
the three pairs spans the masculine/feminine axis**: Point(M)&Shape(F),
Line(M)&Wave(F), Angle(M)&Curve(F).

So there are at least three groupings of the same six, for different purposes:
3 pairs (rotation class), 3+3 (polarity), 4+2 (base vs modulation). Reporting a
single "count" collapses three real structures into one number — which is a
better reason for `UWS-PRIMITIVE-COUNT` being malformed than the one recorded.
**F2 stands as a partial read; do not cite it alone.**

findings.title: the pairing is DERIVED from rotational behaviour
findings.text:
`UniversalSymbology-3CoreSymbolMergers.png` states the rule in its own words,
and it matches F5 exactly:

- **Point & Shape** — "are Geometrically Balanced"  → rotation-invariant
- **Line & Wave** — "change depending on Orientation" → orientation-bearing
- **Angle & Curve** — "are Modulations"               → carry direction *and* extent

So the three pairs are not a stylistic grouping. They are the three classes a
mark can fall into with respect to rotation. **This is the most important
structural fact found so far** and it is checkable by anyone with a protractor.

findings.title: the rotation table is the strongest structural document in the set
findings.text:
`UniversalSymbology-Base6_rotary.png` (3278x2125). Six features × eight
orientations (up, down, right, left, and the four diagonals). The row behaviour
is the finding:

| feature | under rotation |
|---|---|
| **Point** | **invariant** — identical dot in all eight columns |
| **Shape** (circle) | **invariant** — identical circle in all eight columns |
| Angle | 8 distinct forms |
| Line | 8 distinct forms |
| Wave | 8 distinct forms |
| Curve | 8 distinct forms |

This is a **provable geometric fact**, not an assignment: a point is
0-dimensional and a circle is rotationally symmetric, so neither carries
orientation. The other four do. **Candidate Tier 0.**

findings.title: modality is waveform, with a signal-theory basis
findings.text:
Mk3 "Modalities Base 3": Cardinal/Angular → triangle wave, Fixed/Linear →
square wave, Mutable/Curvilinear → sine wave. This is the sharp/flat/round
distinction in the conformance test, but grounded in waveform rather than
asserted as a shape convention.

findings.title: elements are compositional (candidate Tier 1)
findings.text:
Triangle orientation × presence of a bar gives four elements:
up = Fire, up+bar = Air, down = Water, down+bar = Earth. Two binary features,
four outcomes, exactly saturated. Matches what `tools/arkana_render.py` already
implements and `tests/test_arkana_conformance.py` validates against the app.

findings.title: "Base 6 (4+2)": Angle and Curve look like operators, not primitives
findings.text:
The Mk3 "Fundamental Symbol Features" grid crosses:

- **Points, Lines, Waves, Shapes** — four base features
- **Angles, Curves** — shown as *applied to* the others: "Angled Lines, Angled
  Points, Angled Shapes, Angled Waves"; "Curved Lines, Curved Points, Curved
  Shapes, Curved Waves"

If right, this reconciles the count dispute: 4 base + 2 operators = 6 marks, and
whether you say 4 or 6 depends on whether operators count as primitives. That
would explain *why* `UWS-PRIMITIVE-COUNT` records the question as malformed,
rather than only *that* it does. **Awaiting owner confirmation.**

findings.title: the bracketed roles are not the semantic categories
findings.text:
Mk3 top-left panel gives each feature a bracketed role:

```
Point [Core]    Angle [Alpha]    Line [Order]
Wave  [Chaos]   Curve [Omega]    Shape [Void]
```

These are **not** Existence / Relation / Quality / Process / Concept. So the
`Point = Existence` identity retired today as `PRIMITIVE-SEMANTIC-IDENTITY`
appears to originate in later wiki/site prose, not in the drawn system.
*To confirm against Mk1/Mk2 and the text primers before treating as established.*
